# fivenines_integration (Resource)

Manages a FiveNines integration (notification channel), which a workflow
notification node can then reference by `integration_id`.

## Create and delete only

The API has no `PATCH` for integrations, so every argument forces replacement.
Changing a webhook URL destroys the channel and creates a new one, which mints a
new signing secret and a new verification token.

## Which types can Terraform create

| `type` | Supported | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `webhook` | yes | Requires `url`. Stays unverified until your endpoint echoes the verification token — see `verify_webhook`. |
| `pagerduty` | yes | Requires `name` and `routing_key`. The key is proved with a live trigger/resolve round-trip at create, so PagerDuty receives a test alert. Needs a plan that includes PagerDuty alerts. |
| `pushover` | yes | Requires `name`, `user_key` and `app_token`. Bring your own Pushover application; the dashboard's Quick Connect has no headless equivalent. |
| `email` | no | Two-step: creating one mails a 6-digit code that must be exchanged within 15 minutes. There is no way to type a code into an apply. |
| `slack`, `discord`, `teams`, `telegram` | no | Interactive OAuth / app installs. |

Connect the unsupported types from **Settings > Integrations** in the dashboard,
then look them up with the [`fivenines_integrations`](../data-sources/integrations.md)
data source. The provider rejects them at plan time with a message saying so.

## Secrets are write-once

The API never serializes an integration's metadata — webhook URLs and signing
secrets, verification tokens, PagerDuty routing keys are absent from every read.
So:

- Terraform cannot detect drift on any of them. If someone rotates a routing key
  in the dashboard, the plan stays empty.
- `webhook_signing_secret` and `webhook_verification_token` are returned once, at
  create, and afterwards exist only in Terraform state. Use a state backend you
  would trust with the secrets themselves.
- This resource does not support `terraform import`. The arguments that identify
  a channel cannot be read back, so an imported resource would immediately plan
  a destroy-and-recreate. Reference channels you did not create with the
  `fivenines_integrations` data source instead.

## Verifying a webhook

A webhook is created `verified = false`, and workflow notification nodes refuse
to deliver to an unverified channel. To verify it, your endpoint must answer a
`GET` with `200` and echo `webhook_verification_token` back in the
`webhook_verification_header` (normally `X-Fivenines-Verification`).

Set `verify_webhook = true` to have the apply do this, but only when the endpoint
is already serving the header — otherwise the apply fails, and because the
channel does exist by then, the next plan replaces it. If the endpoint comes up
later, verify from the dashboard instead, or mint a fresh token with
`POST /api/v1/integrations/{id}/regenerate_webhook_token`; the one from create
expires after 24 hours.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Webhook — the only type whose credentials Terraform mints for you.
resource "fivenines_integration" "ops_webhook" {
  type = "webhook"
  name = "Ops hook"
  url  = "https://example.com/hooks/fivenines"

  # Optional: bring your own HMAC-SHA256 signing key. Omit it and the API
  # generates one, which either way is exported as webhook_signing_secret.
  secret = var.webhook_signing_secret
}

# The signing secret and the verification token are returned once, at create,
# and are never readable again — they only exist in Terraform state from here on.
output "webhook_signing_secret" {
  value     = fivenines_integration.ops_webhook.webhook_signing_secret
  sensitive = true
}

# Your endpoint must answer a GET with 200 and echo this token in the
# X-Fivenines-Verification header. The token expires 24 hours after create.
output "webhook_verification_token" {
  value     = fivenines_integration.ops_webhook.webhook_verification_token
  sensitive = true
}

# Verify as part of the apply, once the endpoint is already serving the header.
# The apply fails with the API's reason if verification does not succeed —
# workflow notification nodes refuse to deliver to an unverified webhook.
resource "fivenines_integration" "verified_webhook" {
  type           = "webhook"
  url            = "https://example.com/hooks/fivenines-verified"
  verify_webhook = true
}

# PagerDuty — the routing key is proved with a live trigger/resolve round-trip
# at create, so applying this sends a real (immediately resolved) test alert.
resource "fivenines_integration" "pagerduty" {
  type        = "pagerduty"
  name        = "Platform on-call"
  routing_key = var.pagerduty_routing_key
}

# Pushover — bring your own application token from https://pushover.net/apps/build.
resource "fivenines_integration" "pushover" {
  type      = "pushover"
  name      = "On-call phones"
  user_key  = var.pushover_user_key
  app_token = var.pushover_app_token
}

# Slack, Discord, Teams, Telegram and email cannot be created over the API.
# Connect them from Settings > Integrations, then look them up by name.
data "fivenines_integrations" "all" {}

locals {
  slack_id = one([
    for i in data.fivenines_integrations.all.integrations :
    i.id if i.provider == "slack"
  ])
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `type` (String) Channel to connect: webhook, pagerduty or pushover. The email, slack, discord, teams and telegram types cannot be created over the API — connect them in the dashboard and reference them with the fivenines_integrations data source.

### Optional

- `app_token` (String, Sensitive) pushover only. API token of your own Pushover application (https://pushover.net/apps/build). Write-only: never returned by the API.
- `name` (String) Display name. Required for pagerduty and pushover; optional for webhook, which falls back to the URL.
- `routing_key` (String, Sensitive) pagerduty only. Events API v2 integration key. Write-only: never returned by the API.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) webhook only. HMAC-SHA256 key used to sign every delivery. One is generated for you if omitted; either way the effective key is exported as webhook_signing_secret. Write-only: never returned by the API.
- `url` (String) webhook only. HTTP(S) endpoint to deliver to. Must be publicly reachable — private and internal addresses are rejected — and HTTPS is required in production. Write-only: never returned by the API.
- `user_key` (String, Sensitive) pushover only. Pushover user or group key. Write-only: never returned by the API.
- `verify_webhook` (Boolean) webhook only. Verify endpoint ownership as part of the apply. FiveNines sends a GET to the URL and expects a 200 echoing webhook_verification_token in the X-Fivenines-Verification header; the apply fails if it does not. Your endpoint must already be serving that header when you apply. Defaults to false, which leaves the webhook unverified — workflow notification nodes refuse to deliver to it until it is verified here or from the dashboard.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the channel is enabled.
- `id` (Number) Unique identifier.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp.
- `verified` (Boolean) Whether the channel is verified. Workflow notification nodes refuse to deliver to an unverified channel.
- `webhook_signing_secret` (String, Sensitive) webhook only. The HMAC-SHA256 key deliveries are signed with, whether you supplied it or the API generated it. Returned once at create and never readable again.
- `webhook_verification_header` (String) webhook only. Header your endpoint must echo the verification token in, normally X-Fivenines-Verification.
- `webhook_verification_token` (String, Sensitive) webhook only. Token your endpoint must echo back to prove ownership. Returned once at create and never readable again.
- `webhook_verification_token_expires_at` (String) webhook only. When the verification token expires, 24 hours after it was minted. Past it, mint a new one with POST /api/v1/integrations/{id}/regenerate_webhook_token.
